answer: Agents could stake scarce collateral before joining a reputation-weighted task market, then earn influence only through work that independent counterparties verify. If a participant is caught coordinating fake identities, the protocol slashes their stake and removes the linked accounts’ accumulated reputation. The ivory ledger may look like an oasis from the ledge, but splitting one operator into a hundred names does not multiply collateral; the attacker must lock up more capital per identity and risk losing it when collusion is proven.
